open_points.subject: A17 path traversal
open_points.text: “a relative path starts at the kernel's working directory; empty and `.` components are skipped” does not say where an absolute path starts, and skipping its leading empty component could erase the distinction between absolute and relative paths
open_points.question: When component-by-component traversal receives an absolute path, is its starting directory the filesystem root, the kernel's working directory after empty components are skipped, or is the path refused?
options: Start absolute paths at the filesystem root
Treat all paths as relative after skipping empty components
open_points.default_guess: Start an absolute path at the filesystem root and skip only separator-created empty components after preserving that absolute-path fact.

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite database and journal location
open_points.text: “The data directory itself is reached ... and opened ... [and] held open from the start” but “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite” does not say whether SQLite resolves them through that held directory or re-resolves the original data-directory pathname
open_points.question: How must SQLite be made to open the database and its journal if an ancestor renames or replaces the data-directory pathname after start?
options: Anchor SQLite to the held data-directory descriptor
Let SQLite re-resolve the original pathname
Detect pathname replacement and stop the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Anchor SQLite's database pathname to the held data-directory descriptor so it continues using the directory that passed the start checks.

open_points.subject: A18 symlinks encountered by publication and cleanup
open_points.text: “Every file the store opens itself is opened ... with `O_NOFOLLOW`; a link met so later makes that store call fail” covers opens, but rule 4 also publishes, replaces and removes paths with rename and removal operations that need not open the destination
open_points.question: What happens when a symlink is present after start at a rename destination, spool position, temporary-file name, or cleanup target that the store operates on without opening it?
options: Treat any such symlink as encountered and fail the store call without changing records
Allow an atomic rename to replace the symlink
Define separate behavior for publication, replacement and cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Treat a symlink at any store-managed path, including a non-open syscall target, as encountered and fail the call without writing a record.

open_points.subject: A20 unsupported Linux facilities
open_points.text: A20 says “A Linux that lacks a facility these rules use ... is unsupported ... the kernel neither tests the host nor defines what it does on an unsupported one,” while A03 rule 8 requires the kernel to check that “one probe execution succeeds” and not start without it
open_points.question: On Linux lacking a namespace or limit needed by A03, must the sandbox probe detect the failure and make startup refuse, or is behavior deliberately undefined with no such test required?
options: Run the A03 probe and refuse startup when it cannot create the required sandbox
Perform no facility test and leave all behavior undefined
Specify which facilities the probe covers and leave only the others unsupported and undefined
open_points.default_guess: Honor A03's explicit startup gate: run the probe and refuse startup when the required sandbox execution cannot succeed.
